sources.entry: Umami - Simple, fast, privacy-focused alternative to Google Analytics. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Nodejs/Docker
Umami | Simple, fast, privacy-focused alternative to Google Analytics

summary.one_liner: Umami is a self-hostable, privacy-first web analytics platform that tracks traffic, campaigns, behavior, conversions, and revenue without cookies.
summary.what_it_does: Umami is an analytics platform for websites, positioned as a privacy-focused alternative to Google Analytics. The README says it covers traffic, campaigns, behavior, conversions, and revenue in one place, and that it uses no cookies. It can be self-hosted or used as a cloud service. Installation from source requires Node.js 18.18+ and a PostgreSQL database (v12.14+), configured through a DATABASE_URL in an .env file. Docker images and a docker compose file (which runs Umami with PostgreSQL) are provided. Optional settings include API_URL for internal UI API calls, TWO_FACTOR_ENCRYPTION_KEY to enable two-factor authentication, and MCP_ENABLED to expose an /mcp endpoint authenticated with API keys. The build step creates database tables and a default admin login.
how_to_run: git clone the repository and cd into umami
Or use Docker: docker compose up -d
notable: Cookie-free tracking, positioned as a privacy-first alternative to Google Analytics
Can be self-hosted or used in the cloud
Optional MCP endpoint for API-key-authenticated access
Optional two-factor authentication with a configurable encryption key
Official Docker image and compose file with PostgreSQL
caveats: Requires a PostgreSQL database and Node.js 18.18+ for source installs
Default build creates an admin account with a known default password (admin/umami) that should be changed
Two-factor authentication cannot be enabled until TWO_FACTOR_ENCRYPTION_KEY is set
MCP endpoint is disabled by default
